Judgment :

1. Heard finally with consent of the parties.
2.

Appeal is preferred by the insurance company challenging judgment and award passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Latur in Motor Accident Claim Petition 3 FA.3039-2019.odt No.226 of 2015 awarding compensation of Rs.40,98,934/- with interest @ Rs.6% to be paid jointly and severally by appellant and others.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition 3 FA.3039-2019.odt No.226 of 2015
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Respondent Nos.1 to 7 are the claimants.
3. Ravindra Digambar Waghchaure died in accident on 29.11.2014 due to head-on collision between motorcycle of which he was pillion rider and offending jeep Sumo.
He was working as Junior Technician in MSEDCL.
A charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
4. The claim is contested by the appellant/insurance company as well as other respondents on the ground of contributory negligence, entitlement and quantum.
No oral evidence was led by the appellant.
The claimants examined two witnesses.

The deceased was held to be earning Rs.30,564/-
per month as salary considering the basic pay and the allowances.
He was held to be of 46 years at the relevant time.
For loss of consortium, sum of Rs.40,000/- is found to be payable.
The quantum is arrived at Rs.40,98,934/-.

2 5.

Learned counsel Mr. Mohit Deshmukh appearing for the appellant/insurance company has formulated following submissions ;
4 FA.3039-2019.odt (i) The quantum has been determined incorrectly by adding allowances also which is impermissible.
The quantum is exorbitant and unreasonable.

(ii) Respondents/claimants suppressed that they received compensation under Employees'
Compensation Act.
As per Section 167, they are entitled to receive compensation only once.
(iii) The Tribunal overlooked that it's a case of contributory negligence considering spot panchnama and other material.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents would support impugned judgment and award.
It is submitted that the monthly salary has been proved by pay slip by the evidence of Ajay Pithale.
There is no mistake in calculating the quantum.

The claimants are contended to be entitled to 10%
increase in the loss of consortium.

It is submitted that employer suo motu paid the compensation and claimants are entitled to receive compensation under Motor Vehicles Act as well as Employees'
Compensation Act.

5 FA.3039-2019.odt 7. Learned counsel for the respondents sought reliance on the judgment of Raghuvir Singh Matolya and others Vs. Hari Singh Malviya and others ; (2009) 15 Supreme Court Cases 363, National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Mannat Johal and others ; (2019) 15 Supreme Court Cases 260 and Sebastiani Lakra and others Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. and another ; (2019) 17 Supreme Court Cases 465.
8.

sentences.text: I have considered rival submissions of the parties.
I have also gone through record and proceedings.
Factum of accident and death are not disputed.
The deceased was permanent employee of M.S.E.D.C.L. and drawing salary is also not disputed.
The Tribunal recorded that deceased Ravindra was drawing salary of Rs.30,564/- per month.
9. Considering the oral evidence of C.W.2 and the pay slip at Exh.59, the monthly income of the deceased is arrived at.
The pay slip at Exh.59 shows basic of Rs.12,260/- and dearness allowance as Rs.12,260/-.
It further refers to previous arrears of four installments of Rs.957/- of the dearness allowance.
The Tribunal did not consider the arrears of the dearness allowance in the gross salary.
The allowance towards electricity charges 6 FA.3039-2019.odt of Rs.165/-, SP.

Comp. allowance of Rs.95/-, heavy duty allowance of Rs.50/-, risk allowance of Rs.140/-, Special OT allowance of Rs.185/-, Trans Asstt. allowance of Rs.125/- and washing allowance of Rs.60/- are for the personal enjoyment and benefit of the employee which cannot form the loss of income.
Those are provided for benefit, safety and comfort of the individual.
Those should have been excluded while arriving at monthly salary.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant seeks to rely on the judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Lauretta Shashi Mogale and others in First Appeal No.1067 of 2018 rendered by learned Single Judge.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Lauretta Shashi Mogale and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through para No.6.2.
In that case also, it was held that arrears and the allowances should have been deducted from the salary.
The reliance inter alia is placed on judgment of Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company.

Further reliance is placed on the judgment of The New India Assurance Company Ltd. Vs. Surekha Bhagwan Desle in First Appeal No.3027 of 2019 to buttress that arrears of dearness allowance cannot be included in the monthly salary for determining loss of income.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd. Vs. Surekha Bhagwan Desle
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I find substance in the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant.
The monthly salary ought to have been to the tune of Rs.25,976/- aggregating Rs.12,260/- + 12,260/- + 1226/- + 230/-.
The finding that monthly salary was Rs.30,564/- is erroneous.
12. It has come on record through the extract of service book of the deceased that the claimants were paid amount of Rs.6,65,160/- towards compensation under Employees' Compensation Act.
The claimants should have disclosed this fact.
But they cannot be non suited for the suppression.
13. I have gone through Section 161 of Motor Vehicles Act which gives option to the claimants to claim compensation in either of the Act.
It was brought to the notice of the Tribunal that the claimants were being paid compensation by the employer.
It reveals that the compensation was paid by the employer suo motu.
The claimants should have chosen the compensation which they aspire for.
The payment of compensation by employer albeit suo motu does not entitle them to claim both the compensation.

14. My attention is adverted by learned counsel Mr. 8 FA.3039-2019.odt Deshmukh to judgment of Apex Court in judgment of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Dyamavva and others ; (2013) 9 Supreme Court Cases 406.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Dyamavva and others ; (2013) 9 Supreme Court Cases 406
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case also, employer had paid compensation suo motu under Workmen's Compensation Act and the claimants had claimed distinct compensation under Motor Vehicles Act.
It is held that compensation paid under the Workmen's Compensation Act needs to be deducted.
The reference to paragraph Nos.18 and 19 are relevant.
15. In the present matter also amount of Rs.6,65,160/- is required to be deducted which is not done by the Tribunal.
It is rightly submitted that the quantum determined by the Tribunal is exorbitant and illegal.
16. I have gone through spot panchnama.
The oral evidence and the documentary evidence of the police papers would suggest that driver of the offending vehicle is responsible.
He is facing criminal action also.
The insurance company did not lead any evidence.
I do not find any merit in the submissions of Mr. Deshmukh that contributory negligence has been proved.
17. The Tribunal considered Rs.40,000/- towards the loss of consortium.

As the accident was prior to decision of Supreme 9 FA.3039-2019.odt Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Thr Its ... vs Savita Ravindra Waghchaure And Ors on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164664319/
4 Sethi & ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, the claim of the respondents for increase of 10% cannot be accepted.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Thr Its ... vs Savita Ravindra Waghchaure And Ors on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, I have come across a flaw.
There are seven dependents and the amount of Rs.40,000/- only was allotted for loss of consortium.
This is not in accordance with law.
The respondents/claimants are entitled to get Rs.40,000 x 7 = Rs.2,80,000/- towards loss of consortium.
18. I have gone through the judgment cited by the respondents in the matter of Raghuvir Singh (supra).
The proposition cannot be disputed.
The dearness allowance and house rent allowance are to be included in the salary.
Further reliance is placed on the judgment of Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Vs. Mannat Johal (supra) .
I have gone through the parameters culled down in paragraph No.12.
But, no endeavour is made as to how those are said to be violated in present case.
Further reliance is placed on the judgment of Supreme Court in case of Sebastiani Lakra (supra).
It is not shown that as to how there is violation of principles laid down therein.
The judgments cited by the respondents referred above would not help the respondents to defend the quantum arrived 10 FA.3039-2019.odt at in the impugned judgment.
19. It transpires that appellant company deposited Rs.49,88,270/-.
Out of that Rs.30,00,000/- was disbursed to the claimants.
They are entitled to receive the balance amount by adjusting the modified quantum.
20. The amount of Rs.6,65,160/- is required to be deducted.
Simultaneously, amount of Rs.2,80,000/- needs to be replaced for loss of consortium.
Considering the monthly salary of Rs.25,976/- loss of dependency would come to Rs.35,82,215/-.

Respondents are entitled to receive following compensation :
 (a) Loss of dependency - Rs. 35,82,215/-
(b) Loss of consortium - Rs. 02,80,000/-
( c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-

( d ) Loss towards estate - Rs. 15,000/-
 Total - Rs. 38,92,215/-
Accordingly, first appeal is allowed partly in following terms :
(i) First appeal is partly allowed.
11 FA.3039-2019.odt  (ii) Impugned judgment is modified and the quantum  of Rs.40,98,934/- shall be replaced by  Rs.32,27,055/-.
